chunks: Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a slave who married without the permission of his master. He said: “That is up to the master; if he wishes, he approves it, and if he wishes, he separates them.”

I said: “May Allah rectify you, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and their companions say that the basis of the marriage is invalid, so the master’s approval does not render it lawful.” He said: “He only disobeyed his master and did not disobey Allah; so if he approves it for him, then it is valid.”

key_terms.إِجَازَةُ: ratification or approval after the act
key_terms.إِذْنِ: permission or authorization required for the act
key_terms.فَاسِدٌ: invalid or unsound in legal status
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٍ: an owned slave or bondsman under a master's authority
key_terms.ٱلسَّيِّدِ: the master whose approval or refusal determines the ruling here

ai.seo_question: Is a slave’s marriage without the master’s permission automatically invalid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave who contracts marriage without his master's permission. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that the marriage is not void in itself; rather, its continuation depends on the master's approval, because the disobedience was toward the master, not toward Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4862 - Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a slave who married without the permission of his master.
Imam (as) replied: "This matter is up to the master. If he wishes, he can approve the marriage, and if he wishes, he can separate them."

I said: "May Allah (swt) rectify your affairs! Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, and their companions say that the marriage is invalid from the outset, and the master's approval does not make it lawful."
Imam (as) responded: "He only disobeyed his master but did not disobey Allah (swt). Therefore, if the master approves it, the marriage becomes valid."
